newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Single currency, Mideast top Davos Forum agenda.
newsitem.headline: Single currency, Mideast top Davos Forum agenda.

text.p: Movers and shakers from politics and business converged on a Swiss Alpine resort on Thursday for the annual World Economic Forum, with this year's focus on Europe's single currency plan and Middle East peace.

Billed by organisers as the most important business summit in the world, the 27th annual meeting of the week-long Forum lets nearly 2,000 leaders of countries and companies rub elbows in a conference centre nestling under snowy peaks.

Key figures due to take part include European Commission President Jacques Santer, Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, South African President Nelson Mandela and Middle East "partners in peace" Benjamin Netanyahu and Yasser Arafat.
Talks on launching the single currency in 1999 feature the finance ministers of France, Germany, Spain and Britain.

European central bankers taking part in Forum sessions include Jean-Claude Trichet, governor of the Bank of France; Bundesbank board member Johann-Wilhelm Gaddum, and Howard Davies, deputy governor of the Bank of England.

Other key financial figures attending the Forum include U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers; Akira Nagashima, deputy governor of the Bank of Japan, and Yves-Thibault de Silguy, European Commissioner in charge of monetary affairs.
On the political front, the highlight will be a panel discussion set for Sunday afternoon that brings Netanyahu, Arafat and Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak onto the same podium.
From Moscow, Chernomyrdin was set to arrive on Thursday. President Boris Yeltsin's chief of staff, Anatoly Chubais, was also scheduled to attend.
Access to such top leaders is why companies spend thousands of dollars for the right to send senior executives to Davos.

"People are increasingly concerned about Russia and they will see Russian officials here. The Middle East is going to be a big issue and a number of the major players in the Middle East are going to be here," Robert Hormats, vice-chairman of Goldman Sachs International, told Reuters Financial Television
Other prominent figures to address this year's meeting are new United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan and Newt Gingrich, speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives.
Gingrich will address the Forum on Sunday in his first major speech abroad since he took up the key post following the Republican electoral victories of 1994.
The conference is also becoming a backdrop for talks on Switzerland's row with Jewish groups over demands that Holocaust victims get quick compensation for their wartime suffering.
Swiss President Arnold Koller, his country under fire from Jewish groups who accuse it of cynically profiting from World War Two, is due to meet Netanyahu in Davos on Friday.
